The story is tightly unified around the narrator's perception of Q's seemingly effortless competence and grace. The beginning establishes Q's composed, conflict-free persona in college and the narrator's secret desire to "catch him failing" because they believed intimacy required finding a contradiction in someone's public character. This directly sets up the middle of the story ten years later, where the narrator overhears Q at the pool struggling to fire a colleague and failing to be firm out of a mix of kindness and conflict-avoidance. Finally, this leads logically to the ending, where Q also disappoints his daughter by missing her dive. Having finally witnessed Q's human flaws and failures, the narrator realizes there is no satisfaction or "prepared response" in it, and chooses to leave Q to his life and his quiet amends with his daughter rather than intruding. Every scene and piece of dialogue directly serves this central character study and thematic arc.
